correctness.rationale: The primary definitions and theorem were reconstructed. Algebra gives the source orthogonality condition exactly as \((I-S^{-1})X=0\), while duality is exactly \(X=0\). The kernel identity \(\ker(I-S^{-1})=\ker(S-I)\) proves the point-spectrum boundary. The \(\mathbb C^2\) counterexample has exact frame bounds, exact orthogonality, and mixed operator \(\operatorname{diag}(2,1)\), so it refutes the converse without numerical approximation. The converse-of-the-boundary construction uses the bounded right inverse \(T_\Lambda^*S^{-1}\) and realizes every nonzero defect into the \(1\)-eigenspace by a \(g\)-Bessel family.
